issues.failure_explanation: The consistency term $b_\Gamma(v,v;v_f,0) = -\int_\Sigma (2\mu_f\eps(v_f)n_S\cdot n_S)(v_f\cdot n_S+v_r\cdot n_P+w_s\cdot n_P)$ is indefinite; by (I1) it is bounded below by the two NEGATIVE terms $-\delta_1 C_{tr}^2\mu_f\|\eps(v_f)\|^2 - \frac{\mu_f}{\delta_1}\sum h_E^{-1}\|jump\|^2$, not by the positive quantities displayed (take the strain trace and the jump pointwise aligned to make $b_\Gamma<0$). Those negative terms are absorbed by the Nitsche penalty only under the condition $\gamma > (\varsigma+1)(\hat\epsilon_f')^{-1}$ (used in Theorem E+H), which is missing from the hypotheses of this lemma and of Lemma invertibilty that cites it.

failure_location.quote: the linear operator $\mathbf{A}$ is continuous and elliptic for any given $ \bw_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the penalty condition $\gamma > (\varsigma+1)(\hat\epsilon_f')^{-1}$ (with the associated smallness of $\hat\epsilon_f'$) to the hypotheses of Lemma coercivity-continuity and Lemma invertibilty, flip the signs in the displayed lower bound, and absorb the negative consistency term with the penalty.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, ellipticity of A is unproved (the displayed lower bound is false and the needed penalty hypothesis is absent). All applications (Theorems E+H, thm:added-1, lem:added-1, appendix_fully) already impose the penalty condition, so no final result loses validity.
issues.title: Coercivity lemma omits the Nitsche penalty condition and states a wrong-sign lower bound for the interface consistency term
issues.why_classification: The repair is a forced sign correction plus addition of a hypothesis already imposed in every application; the method, conclusions, rates, and scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma usual_inf only lower-bounds the supremum over the FULL space $\mathbf{V}_h$. The proof lower-bounds $\sup_{\mathbf{V}_{h,0}}$ by $\xi_1\|q_h\|$ 'by virtue of Lemma usual_inf', but restricting the test space to the subspace $\mathbf{V}_{h,0}$ (zero normal jump on $\Sigma$) can only decrease the supremum, so the inequality does not follow. A uniform discrete inf-sup for the form containing the interface term $\int_\Sigma q_h^S(v_f\cdot n_S+v_r\cdot n_P+w_s\cdot n_P)$ requires a genuinely new argument (e.g., a Fortin operator preserving the constraint); in the plain $L^2$ pressure norm the interface trace term is not a uniformly controlled perturbation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the discrete inf-sup for the coupled operator by a Fortin-type construction compatible with the interface constraint (or in interface-weighted norms with a perturbation argument); independently, give a short direct proof of $\ker(\mathbf{B}^T)=\{0\}$ for the existence/uniqueness chain.
issues.overall_effect: The h-uniform inf-sup for $\mathbf{B}$ is unestablished. Consequently the quantitative pressure estimates in the stability lemma (lem:added-1) and the error theorem (appendix_fully), the pressure uniqueness in Theorem E+H, and — as written, via Lemma invertibilty — the invertibility of $\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N}$ used for existence in E+H, thm:added-1 and thm:added-2 all lack a valid proof. (The kernel-triviality needed for the existence chain is separately recoverable; the quantitative pressure bounds are not.)
issues.title: inf-sup proof for the interface-coupled divergence operator restricts the supremum to a constrained subspace without justification
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a contained but nontrivial inf-sup argument (a new Fortin-type lemma). Nothing in the source shows the statement is false, and standard techniques are expected to restore a recognizably comparable result without changing the method, rates, or regime.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the stated hypotheses the implication fails. Counterexample within the same block structure: $\mathbf{A}=((0,1),(-1,0))$ (skew-symmetric, so $x^T\mathbf{A}x=0\ge 0$ with trivial kernel), $\mathbf{B}=(1,0)$, $\mathbf{C}=(0)$. Then $\ker\mathbf{A}\cap\ker\mathbf{B}=\{0\}$ and $\ker\mathbf{C}\cap\ker\mathbf{B}^T=\{0\}$, but the assembled $3\times3$ matrix has identical second and third rows and is singular. The energy argument $x^T\mathbf{A}x+y^T\mathbf{C}y=0$ forces $x\in\ker\mathbf{A}$ only if $\mathbf{A}$ is symmetric PSD or positive definite; the needed hypothesis is $\mathbf{A}$ positive definite, which Lemma invertibilty supplies via coercivity. No proof is given in the source.

failure_location.quote: if the matrices $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ are positive semi-definite and $\operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{A}) \cap \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{B}) = \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{C}) \cap \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{B}^T) = \{0\}$, then the matrix $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$ is invertible for any given $ \bw_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to '$\mathbf{A}$ positive definite' and supply the standard two-line energy argument ($x^T\mathbf{A}x+y^T\mathbf{C}y=0 \Rightarrow x=0$, $y\in\ker\mathbf{C}\cap\ker\mathbf{B}^T$).
issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary lemma is literally false as stated; its applications (Theorem E+H, and the matrix argument of Theorem thm:added-2) remain valid because there $\mathbf{A}$ is positive definite by the coercivity result.
issues.title: Auxiliary invertibility lemma is false as stated: positive semi-definiteness of A does not imply invertibility of the saddle-point matrix
issues.why_classification: A single forced hypothesis correction, already satisfied in every application, plus a routine omitted proof; no mathematical content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: According to the DAE theory (see \cite[Theorem~2.3.1]{MR1101809}), if the matrix pencil \(s\,\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}\) is nonsingular for some \(s\neq 0\) and the initial data are consistent, then the system \eqref{mixed-primal} admits a solution.

issues.failure_explanation: No $\partial_t p^{\mathrm{S}}$ term occurs anywhere in the form $E$, so the $p_h^{\mathrm{S}}$ column of the mass matrix $\mathbf{M}$ (called $E$ here) is identically zero; $\mathbf{M}$ is singular and the semi-discrete system is a genuine DAE with an algebraic constraint (the incompressibility/Nitsche constraint row $-(\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}})^*u_f+(\mathcal{C}_{f,\Gamma})^*u_f+(\mathcal{C}_{p,\Gamma})^*u_r+(\mathcal{C}_{s,\Gamma})^*\partial_t y_s=\mathcal{F}_{p^{\mathrm{S}}}$). 'No zero rows' is not a criterion for absence of algebraic constraints, and the ensuing assertion that the initial values 'are consistent and do not lead to any incompatibility issues' is unsupported: the cited DAE theorem requires consistent initial data, i.e., the discrete constraint equations at $t=0$ restrict the initial approximations (a discrete divergence constraint on $\bu_{f,h}(0)$ coupled to $\bu_{r,h}(0)$, $\bu_{s,h}(0)$), which is neither imposed nor verified.

failure_location.quote: The matrix \(E\) has no zero rows, which implies that the system has no algebraic constraints.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the false assertion and add the standard hypothesis that the initial data satisfy the discrete constraint equations (e.g., via a constraint-preserving projection); regularity of the pencil ($\mathbf{M}+\mathbf{N}$ invertible) then yields existence and uniqueness for consistent data.
issues.overall_effect: Existence in Theorem E+H is established only for consistent initial data, not for arbitrary 'suitable approximations' as stated; the well-posedness of the fixed-point operator in Theorem thm:added-1 inherits this restriction.
issues.title: Existence proof falsely asserts the semi-discrete DAE has no algebraic constraints; consistency of initial data is not established
issues.why_classification: Restricting to consistent initial data is a standard local condition for DAEs; the method, the theorem's conclusion, and the advertised scope survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed inequality applies a stationary coercivity/inf-sup bound to $\mathcal{A}_{w_1}(z,y)=\bar E(\partial_t z,y)+\bar H(z,y)+c(w_1,z_f,v_f)$ with $z=x_{h1}-x_{h2}$. Tested at $y=z$, $\bar E(\partial_t z,z)$ produces energy terms $\tfrac12\partial_t(\rho_f\|z_f\|^2+\cdots)$ with no definite sign, so no pointwise-in-time coercivity of the claimed form holds: the argument silently drops all time-derivative terms and treats the DAE as an elliptic problem, and the resulting contraction constant $1/3$ is unjustified in any space-time norm. Moreover, Banach's theorem also requires the self-mapping $\mathcal{J}_h(\mathbf{K}_h)\subset\mathbf{K}_h$ — the pointwise gradient bound with the exact constant $\frac{1}{CS_f^2K_f^3}$ — which is never proved (only solvability of the linearized problem is addressed, via 'Lemma E+H'), and $\mathbf{K}_h$ is a set of time-independent functions while $\mathcal{J}_h$ returns a time trajectory, so the map is not even well-defined as declared.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recast the fixed point in a space-time ball (e.g., in $L^2(0,T;\mathbf{V}_{f,h})$), prove the self-mapping from the energy estimate under the small-data condition, and derive the contraction for the difference problem via energy/Gronwall estimates (possibly requiring small $T$ or smaller data); a Schauder-type alternative with the energy estimate is also available.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-1 — well-posedness of the nonlinear semi-discrete Nitsche scheme, one of the paper's advertised main results — is unproved as written; both hypotheses of Banach's fixed-point theorem (self-map and contraction) lack valid arguments.
issues.title: Banach contraction proof treats the time-dependent problem as stationary and never proves that the fixed-point operator maps the ball into itself
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained nontrivial re-argument (space-time fixed-point framework with energy estimates), but it requires no new global proof architecture and the result is expected to survive under the paper's standing small-data assumption.
